vulnerabilities.description: Weak random ID generation using Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 9). This generates predictable IDs for saved calculator results that could be guessed or enumerated.
vulnerabilities.impact: Saved results could be identified and potentially accessed by guessing IDs, though localStorage is client-side only so risk is limited
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use crypto.randomUUID() instead of Math.random() for ID generation

vulnerabilities.description: Content Security Policy allows 'unsafe-inline' for scripts. This weakens protection against inline script injection attacks.
vulnerabilities.impact: Potential for inline script injection if user input is reflected in script tags, though current code properly handles this
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Consider using nonce-based CSP for scripts. If Google Analytics requires unsafe-inline, use proper output encoding for all dynamic content

vulnerabilities.description: Saved calculator results are stored in plaintext localStorage. On shared devices, cached results could be visible to other users.
vulnerabilities.impact: Low - stored data is not sensitive (calculator results, not personal data), but could show previous user's calculations
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Add clear data on logout for shared environments, or add optional encryption for sensitive calculator inputs

vulnerabilities.description: Session data stored in plaintext JSON files in .claude-flow/sessions/. Local file system compromise could expose session context.
vulnerabilities.impact: Low - file system is local-only, but session metadata could be sensitive in some contexts
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Encrypt session files at rest if they contain sensitive user context, or ensure proper file system permissions (chmod 600)

securityPositives.title: No Hardcoded Secrets
securityPositives.description: Excellent practice - no API keys, passwords, or credentials found in source code. All sensitive config uses environment variables.

securityPositives.title: Proper Environment Variable Handling
securityPositives.description: Uses NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix correctly for public values (GA ID, AdSense). No risk of exposing server-side secrets.

securityPositives.title: No SQL Injection Risk
securityPositives.description: Static site with no database queries or SQL code. All data is computed client-side.

securityPositives.title: Safe Command Execution
securityPositives.description: github-safe.js uses spawnSync() instead of shell execution, preventing command injection attacks.

securityPositives.title: Input Validation
securityPositives.description: Helper scripts (memory.js, session.js) validate keys with regex (/^[a-z0-9_]+$/i), preventing injection.

securityPositives.title: Strong HTTP Security Headers
securityPositives.description: Implements HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and XSS-Protection headers.

securityPositives.title: Next.js Built-in Protections
securityPositives.description: Uses Next.js Script component for analytics (properly isolated), not raw inline scripts. React handles XSS by default with proper escaping.

securityPositives.title: No External API Calls
securityPositives.description: Only external dependency is Google Analytics (first-party) and Google AdSense. No third-party API tokens exposed.

riskScoreBasis.mitigatingFactors: Static site with no backend, no user authentication, no sensitive data processing

recommendations.item: Replace Math.random() ID generation with crypto.randomUUID() in saved-results.ts line 22
Review and strengthen CSP policy - consider nonce-based script handling for better inline script protection
Ensure .claude-flow/sessions files have restrictive permissions (chmod 600) to prevent unauthorized local access
recommendations.impact: Protects session metadata from local privilege escalation

recommendations.item: Add optional data clearing mechanism for calculator history on public/shared devices
recommendations.impact: Improves privacy for shared device scenarios

recommendations.impact: Ensures all dependencies are up to date

overallAssessment.summary: This is a well-secured static calculator website. The main risk factors are minor issues with ID generation and CSP policy. The absence of backend services, user authentication, and sensitive data processing significantly reduces the attack surface. No critical vulnerabilities found.
